rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Execution of a lawful bequest made in a recognized manner is obligatory for those concerned besides the testator, whether making it was obligatory, recommended, or merely permissible.
rows.anchor: Esâsı gerek vâcib ve gerek mendub veya mubah olsun ber vech-i ma‘rûf yapılmış olan bir vasiyyet-i meşrû‘anın tenfîzi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After hearing or learning of a lawful bequest, no one may annul or even alter it; anyone who changes it bears the sin of that change.
rows.anchor: vasîlerden [621] veya şâhidlerden veya hükkâm ve sâireden her kim onu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God heard the bequest and knows the public and private words and acts of those who alter it, and will give each the fitting recompense; the warning is emphatic.
rows.anchor: O vasiyeti işitmiştir. Onu tebdil edenleri ve bunların gizli açık kavillerini, fiillerini bilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An executor may carry out a lawful bequest personally heard from the testator without witnesses; the executor’s special authority is stronger than the judge’s general authority.
rows.anchor: vasî olan zâtın bizzat mûsîden işittiği vasiyyet-i meşrû‘ayı bilâ hükmin infaz etmesi câizdir. Vasiyy-i muhtârın velâyet-i hâssası

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Likewise, if the deceased acknowledged a debt before the executor, the executor has a religious duty to pay it when possible without later authorization from heirs or a judge.
rows.anchor: meyyit vasîsi nezdinde bir şahs-ı muayyene borç ikrar etmiş olsa, o vasînin imkân bulunca bu borcu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without evidence, an executor who pays such a debt risks court liability: if heirs deny it, the executor’s bare knowledge cannot prove it and may lead to a judgment requiring repayment.
rows.anchor: vasînin ilm-i mücerredi isbâta kâfî gelmez de talepleri üzerine ikrar ile ilzam ve damâna mahkum edilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier obligation to make a bequest was abrogated, but these verses do not abrogate the continuing duty to execute a lawful bequest.
rows.anchor: evvelki âyetteki vücûb-ı vasiyet mensuh olmakla beraber bu âyette nesih yoktur, vücûb-ı tenfîz bâkīdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuing duty to execute applies only to lawful bequests; an unlawful bequest that embodies injustice rather than recognized right need not be carried out.
rows.anchor: Lâkin bu da meşrû olan vasiyetler hakkındadır. Binâen‘aleyh meşrû olmayan ve mârûfu değil cevri mutazammın bulunan vasiyetlerin infâzı vâcib değildir.

rows.speaker: Şu‘be, Hamza, Kisâî, Ya‘kūb, Halef-i Âşir
rows.claim: These readers transmit the form muvassin, with fatḥa on wāw and a doubled ṣād, from ʿĀṣim’s reading.
rows.anchor: Âsım’dan [622] Şu‘be, Hamza, Kisâî, Ya‘kūb, Halef-i Âşir kıraatlerinde واو’ın fethi ve صاد’ın teşdîdiyle مُّوصٍۢ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A guardian or executor who knows a testator has intentionally or accidentally departed from justice, such as favoring some heirs beyond their shares, may reconcile the parties and restore fairness without sin.
rows.anchor: herhangi bir velî veya vasî bir mûsînin hatâen veya ‘amden haktan meylini, adl ü mâruftan inhirâfını bilir

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports as a mawqūf saying that causing harm through a bequest is among the grave sins; the report is followed by a recitation of 2:229.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas hazretlerinden “اَلْإِْضْرَارُ فِي الْوَصِيَّةِ مِنَ الْكَبَائِرِ: vasiyette ızrâr kebâirdendir” hadîs-i mevkūfu

rows.speaker: Ebû Hureyre
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says a person may do the people of Paradise’s deeds for seventy years yet end in Hell by injustice in a bequest, while a just bequest may bring the opposite ending.
rows.anchor: Ebû Hureyre’den bir hadîs-i nebevîde إِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَيَعْمَلُ بِعَمَلِ أَهْلِ الْجَنَّةِ سَبْعِينَ سَنَةً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an 4:12 excludes a harmful bequest from legal effect, so changing such an unjust bequest carries no sin.
rows.anchor: âyetinde ızrârkârâne vasiyet muteber tutulmamıştır. Binâen‘aleyh bunu tebdilde de günah yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forgives, and may even reward, the sin arising from altering a bequest for the good purpose of reconciliation; this differs from an unjust alteration.
rows.anchor: böyle bir maksad-ı hasen ile tebdîl-i vasiyet ederek ıslâh-ı beyn eden kimsenin bu tebdilden münbâ‘is günahını Allah mağfiret eyler, belki sevab verir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse only grants that a reconciler incurs no sin; it does not command or praise alteration, which is not inherently meritorious and rests on a fallible judgment, so intervention remains risky.
rows.anchor: “sevabdır” demiyor da, “böyle yaparsa ism yoktur” buyuruyor. Çünkü fi‘l-i tebdîl esasen sevab cinsinden olmadığı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Endowments made to take effect after death contain an aspect of bequest; Abū Ḥanīfa derives waqf from bequest, and the warning against alteration also covers necessary endowments.
rows.anchor: vakıflar mâba‘d-i mevte kaldıkları için bir ma‘nâ-yı vasiyeti mutazammındırlar. Hatta İmâm-ı A‘zam vakfı ancak vasiyete tefrî‘etmiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rules about substituting endowments and their conditions derive from the allowance to remedy an unjust bequest; permissible cases are a license rather than a meritorious act.
rows.anchor: İstibdâl-i evkāf ve şurût-ı evkāf meseleleri de فَمَنْ خَافَ âyetine müteferri‘dir. Câiz olanları sevab olarak değil, nihâyet bir ruhsat olarak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Observing divine law requires soul-training, patience, and restraint of the commanding self; fasting is imposed here as an effective spiritual and bodily discipline that renews believers’ inner life.
rows.anchor: iyi bir terbiye-i nefsiyeye mütevakkıftır. Bu ise insanda sabır ve nefs-i emmâreyi zabt ile evâmir-i ilâhiyeye inkıyad melekesini

words: هُدًۭى لِّلنَّاسِ وَبَيِّنَٰتٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْهُدَىٰ وَٱلْفُرْقَانِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elmalılı renders the verse as saying Ramadan is the month when the Qur’an descended as true criterion and clear proofs of guidance to direct humanity.
rows.anchor: O şehr-i Ramazan ki insanları irşâd için hak furkānı, hidâyet delîli beyyineler hâlinde Kur’an onda indirildi.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahr derives from publicity or manifestation: the crescent first appears, and the month is named for the interval from one crescent’s appearance to its next appearance, normally twenty-nine or thirty days.
rows.anchor: “Şehr” esasında şöhretten masdar olup bir şeyi izhar etmek mânasınadır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Astronomers define the month as the interval between two solar conjunctions, but that specialist definition differs from the common lexical sense, measured between the appearances of crescents.
rows.anchor: Müneccimîn bunu kamerin şems ile iki ictimâ‘ı

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujāhid reports that Ramadan is one of God’s names, making shahr Ramadan mean God’s month.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid’den mervî olduğu üzere esmâullahdan bir isimdir. Ve “şehr-i Ramazan” demek

rows.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
rows.claim: A Prophetic report cautions against saying Ramadan came or went, instructing people to say the month of Ramadan; al-Bayhaqī grades this report weak.
rows.anchor: Ve bir hadîs-i nebevî olmak üzere şöyle rivayet edilmiştir: “Ramazan geldi, Ramazan gitti demeyiniz

rows.speaker: Beyhâkî
rows.claim: Al-Bayhaqī considers weak the report that Ramadan is one of God’s names and that one should say the month of Ramadan.
rows.anchor: Ma‘amâfîh Beyhâkî bu hadîse zayıf demiştir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second opinion takes Ramadan, like Rajab and Shaʿbān, as the proper name of a particular month rather than a divine name.
rows.anchor: İkincisi: “Receb”, “şaban”[^3] gibi şehr-i mahsûsun ismidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Ramadan is a divine name, the full phrase shahr Ramadan is a proper name; if Ramadan names the month, the phrase is an explanatory genitive of a general term to a specific one.
rows.anchor: Evvelkine göre “şehr” dâhil olarak شَهْرُ رَمَضَان terkîbinin mecmû‘u bir ism-i ‘alemdir. İkinciye göre isim yalnız “Ramazan”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramadan, Rabīʿ al-Awwal, and Rabīʿ al-Thānī are properly named with shahr, though it is sometimes omitted for brevity; omission for Ramadan is mildly disfavored by Imam Muḥammad but allowed without risk of confusion.
rows.anchor: Tahkīke göre şühûr-ı kameriyeden üçü; şehr-i ramazan, şehr-i rebî‘u’l-evvel, şehr-i rebî‘u’l-âhir, “şehr” kelimesiyle beraber ism-i ‘alemdir.

rows.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
rows.claim: A Prophetic hadith says that whoever fasts Ramadan in faith and seeking reward will have earlier sins forgiven, illustrating omission of shahr before Ramadan.
rows.anchor: Nitekim hadîs-i nebevîde dahi مَنْ صَامَ رَمَضَانَ إِيْمَانًا وَاحْتِسَابًا غُفِرَ لَهُ مَا تَقَدَّمَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nine other lunar-month names are proper nouns without shahr; some also treat Rajab like Ramadan in being named with shahr.
rows.anchor: Mütebâkī dokuz ayın isimleri muharrem, safer, cumâde’l-ûlâ, cumâde’l-âhire, receb, şaban, şevvâl, zilkade, zilhicce “şehr”siz olarak

rows.speaker: Halîl
rows.claim: One etymology derives Ramadan from ramḍā, a late-summer or early-autumn rain that cleanses dust; analogously, Ramadan washes believers’ sins away and purifies their hearts.
rows.anchor: İmam Halîl’den nakl olunduğu üzere yaz sonunda güz mevsiminin evvelinde yağıp yeryüzünü tozdan tathir eden yağmur mânasına رَمْضَى’dan me’huzdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority derive Ramadan from ramad, the heat that makes stones glow: ramida means to burn walking barefoot on hot ground, evoking fasting’s heat and the burning away of sins.
rows.anchor: Ekseriyet kavline göre ramazan رَمَض (ramaz)dan me’huzdur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account says Arab month names were changed according to the seasons; this month, formerly called Nāṭiq, fell in an exceptionally hot season and received the name Ramadan.
rows.anchor: Bir de deniliyor ki Arablar ayların isimlerini lügat-ı kadîmelerinden tahvil ettikleri zaman

rows.speaker: Ezherî
rows.claim: Al-Azharī derives Ramadan from the verb for hammering a sword blade or arrowhead between stones to thin and sharpen it, because Arabs sharpened and prepared weapons during this month.
rows.anchor: Ezherî’den nakl olunan kavildir ki, “ramazan”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Ramadan is truly one of God’s beautiful names, the month takes its name from it with divine mercy and the burning away of sins in view; the name evokes purification, burning, and sharpening.
rows.anchor: “ramazan” isminin esmâ-i hüsnâdan olduğu sahih ise şehr-i Ramazan bizzat bununla tesmiye edilmiş ve bunda bilhassa rahmet-i ilâhiye ile günahların ihtirâkı

rows.speaker: Hz. Peygamber
rows.claim: A Prophetic report describes Ramadan’s beginning as mercy, middle as forgiveness, and end as release from the Fire; the month’s most blessed night also begins the Qur’an’s descent.
rows.anchor: “evveli rahmet, evsatı mağfiret, âhiri ateşten âzâtlık”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Qur’an is God’s speech revealed specifically to Muḥammad, transmitted to us by mass transmission, and written between the two covers of the codices.
rows.anchor: Peygamberimiz Muhammed Mustafa sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’e sûret-i mahsûsada inzal olunup bize tevâtüren nakledilen kelâmullâhın ismidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads Qur’an without hamza in pause and connection, Ḥamza without hamza only in connection, and the remaining readers with hamza; the forms are linked respectively to qarn and qirāʾa.
rows.anchor: İbn Kesîr kıraatinde vakıf ve vasılda ve Hamza kıraatinde yalnız vasılda hemzesiz olarak, mütebâkī kıraatlerde hemze ile okunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With hamza, Qur’an means that which is recited; without hamza, it derives from qarn and denotes parts and contents joined together, mutually confirming and coherent.
rows.anchor: Hemzelisi “kıraat”ten, hemzesizi “karn” maddesindendir, hemze ile مَقْرُوء yani tilâvetle okunan

rows.speaker: İmam Şâfiî
rows.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī says the unhamzated Qur’an is, like Torah and Gospel, an un-derived proper name for God’s scripture.
rows.anchor: İmam Şâfiî hazretleri bunun hemzesiz olarak, Tevrat, İncil gibi bilâ iştikāk ism-i kitâbullâh olduğunu söylemiştir.

rows.speaker: Katâde, Atâ
rows.claim: Qatāda and ʿAṭāʾ say the earlier counted days were an initial fast of three days each month, perhaps with ʿĀshūrāʾ; they differ over whether it began voluntary or obligatory, but agree Ramadan later abrogated it completely.
rows.anchor: Katâde ve Atâ bâlâdaki اَيَّاماً مَعْدُودَات’ın ramazan olmayıp savm-ı evvel, yani her aydan üç gün veya bunlarla beraber yevm-i âşûrâ’dan ibaret bulunduğuna zâhib olmuş

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Mu‘âz
rows.claim: The same earlier-fast account is also attributed to Muʿādh; on it, Ramadan’s obligation is established by this verse’s command rather than by the earlier fasting passage.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Mu‘âz’ın kavli de bu olduğu söylenmiştir. Bunlara göre sıyâm-ı ramazanın delîl-i farziyeti

rows.speaker: cumhûr
rows.claim: The majority hold that the earlier fast was established by Sunna and Ramadan’s obligation began with the earlier command; the counted days mean Ramadan, which this verse explains.
rows.anchor: Lâkin cumhûra göre savm-ı evvel sünnet ile sâbit olmuş ve ramazan orucunun farziyeti ber vech-i bâlâ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُم âyetiyle başlamıştır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counted days prescribed for fasting are the blessed month of Ramadan, in which the Qur’an was sent as guidance for all humanity, with clear proofs of guidance and the Criterion.
rows.anchor: o mübarek şehr-i ramazandır ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inzal means sending down at once, while tanzil means gradual descent; although the Qur’an came gradually over twenty-three years, the verse describes its descent in Ramadan.
rows.anchor: “İnzâl” def‘aten, “tenzîl” de tedrîcen indirmek demekdir. Kur’an yirmi üç senede tedrîcen tenzil buyurulmuş olduğu hâlde

rows.speaker: Ekser müfessirîn
rows.claim: Most exegetes, based on transmitted reports, say the Qur’an descended all at once on Laylat al-Qadr to the lowest heaven or Bayt al-Maʿmūr, then gradually to earth over twenty-three years.
rows.anchor: Ekser müfessirînin rivâyât-ı vâridesine göre Kur’an şehr-i ramazanın “Kadir Gecesi” denilen bir leyle-i mübârekesinde semâ-i dünyâya, Beyt-i Ma‘mûr’a def‘aten inzal

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under this account, the Qur’anic reality manifested collectively in the created realm and nearest heaven on a Ramadan night before its descent to earth.
rows.anchor: hakīkat-i Kur’âniye arza nüzûlünden evvel âlem-i kevnde ve arza en yakın olan semâda bir ramazan gecesi toptan tecellî etmiş

rows.speaker: Muhammed b. İshak
rows.claim: A second interpretation, reported from Muḥammad b. Isḥāq and seeming more apparent to Elmalılı, is that Qur’an began to be revealed in Ramadan, using the whole to indicate a part.
rows.anchor: Kur’an bu ayda inzal olunmaya başladı demektir. Zikr-i kül ve irâde-i cüz kabîlinden mecaz olmakla beraber Muhammed b. İshak’tan mervî ve ma‘amâfîh zâhir gibidir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the beginning-of-revelation interpretation, the first verses of Sūrat al-ʿAlaq at Cave Ḥirāʾ were revealed on Laylat al-Qadr of Ramadan.
rows.anchor: Gār-ı Hirâ’da اِقْرَاْ بِاسْمِ رَبِّكَ âyetinin nüzûlü ramazân-ı şerîfin Kadir gecesine müsâdif olmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation in the heat and pressure of a Ramadan night began a great divine disclosure; 2:153’s call to seek help through patience and prayer offers glad tidings to the distressed.
rows.anchor: mazmûnu üzere ne büyük bir tebşir vardır!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading makes the phrase mean the month in which the Qur’an was revealed; Ramadan alone among months is explicitly named in the Qur’an for divine praise, which helps explain fasting’s assignment to it.
rows.anchor: Kur’an inzal edilmiş bulunan şehr-i ramazan demektir. Fi’l-hakīka Kur’ân-ı azîmü’ş-şân’da bu mübarek aydan başka bilhassa medh-i celîl-i ilâhîye mazhar olarak ismi tasrih edilmiş bir ay yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuhud fundamentally means being present rather than absent, as do shahada and mushahada; al-shahr may be construed as an adverbial of time or as the object of witnessing.
rows.anchor: “Şuhûd” esasen “gıyâb” mukabili huzur demektir ki, “şehadet” ve “müşahede” de bu huzur cümlesindendir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean a person residing in Ramadan, knowing it with certainty, or seeing its crescent; because time cannot literally be seen, witnessing can mean certain knowledge or sight of the crescent.
rows.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh فَمَن شَهِدَ مِنكُمُ ٱلشَّهْرَ şu mânalara muhtemildir. 1. Sizden her kim ramazanda mukīm ise onu tutsun.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resident and certain-knowledge readings concern witnessing part of Ramadan, not its full duration, since the duty is to fast the entire month; the verse leaves means of knowledge unstated.
rows.anchor: şehr mânasınadır. Bu iki mânaya göre esbâb-ı ilim meskûtün anhdır.

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Rāzī says most investigators, including Wāḥidī and the author of al-Kashshāf, choose presence in Ramadan, but he prefers certain knowledge because that reading avoids ellipsis.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “Vâhidî ve sâhib-i Keşşâf gibi ekser muhakkıkīn birinci mânaya zâhib olmuşlardır. Lâkin benim indimde ikinci evlâdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording does not necessarily require sighting the crescent; after seeking the evidence, the means by which Ramadan is known remain unspecified here.
rows.anchor: Hulasâ burada şuhûd-ı hilâl mânası zarûrî değildir. O hâlde esbâb-ı ilim meskûtün ‘anhtır, bunu taharrî etmek lâzım gelecektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If witnessing means residence or certain knowledge and no other text applied, some would allow ijtihad about how to establish the month, including astronomical calculation.
rows.anchor: Bunun için bazıları başka nas yok zannıyla hisâbât-ı nücûmiye ile dahi amel olunabileceğine kāil olmuşlardır.

rows.speaker: cumhûr-ı eslâf
rows.claim: The majority of early authorities reject ijtihad on this matter because other Qur’anic and Prophetic texts specify the evidence for establishing the month.
rows.anchor: Lâkin cumhûr-ı eslâfa göre başkaca nas mevcud olduğundan bu mesele mevrid-i ictihad değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’an 2:189 says crescents are time markers for people, establishing the crescent as the religious indicator of time; Prophetic reports then specify how it is observed.
rows.anchor: Bu bize kat‘iyyen gösterir ki şer‘an vakti tâyin eden delil hilâldir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says a month has twenty-nine days and says not to begin fasting or break it until the crescent is seen; if clouds obscure it, estimate its measure.
rows.anchor: اَلشَّهْرُ تِسْعَةٌ وَعِشْرُونَ لاَ تَصُومُوا حَتَّى تَرَوْهُ وَلاَ تُفْطِرُوا حَتَّى تَرَوْهُ فَإِنْ غُمَّ عَلَيْكُمْ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further report clarifies the instruction for cloudy weather: do not fast until the crescent is seen, and count thirty days when it is obscured.
rows.anchor: لاَ تَصُومُوا حَتَّى تَرَوُا الْهِلَاَلَ فَإِنْ غُمَّ عَلَيْكُمْ فَاقْدُرُوا ثَلَاَثِينَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report directs people to fast and end the fast upon sighting; if cloud or haze blocks the view, they should count thirty.
rows.anchor: صُومُوا لِرُؤْيَتِهِ وَأَفْطِرُوا لِرُؤْيَتِهِ فَإِنْ حَالَ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَ مَنْظَرِهِ سَحَابٌ أَوْ قَتَرَةٌ فَعُدُّوا ثَلَاَثِينَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says to begin Ramadan upon sighting, complete Shaʿbān to thirty if cloud or fog intervenes, and not to preempt Ramadan with a fast on a day of Shaʿbān.
rows.anchor: صُومُوا رَمَضَانَ لِرُؤْيَتِهِ فَإِنْ حَالَ بَيْنَكُمْ غَمَامَةٌ أَوْ ضَبَابَةٌ فَأَكْمِلُوا عِدَّةَ شَهْرِ شَعْبَانَ ثَلَاَثِينَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A final report says months are sometimes thirty and sometimes twenty-nine days: fast and break upon sighting, and count thirty when the sky is cloudy.
rows.anchor: اَلشَّهْرُ هٰكَذَا وَهٰكَذَا الخ: yani ay kâh otuz ve kâh yirmi dokuz olur.
